This is important for the extraction rules below: were votes to carry a separately verifiable ‘participated in view vv’ component, usable in a QC without the vote’s content, the assembler of a V-QC could conceal the positions of correct voters, and the quorum-intersection argument underlying 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌\mathsf{Tips} would fail. The intended semantics, enforced for correct voters by the voting rules below: pjp_{j} has DA-voted for 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,k)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k) for every k∈[1,π​(i)]k\in[1,\pi(i)], and ε​(i)\varepsilon(i) specifies (by payloads, with chain, heights and parents supplied by context, as for proposal entries) a sequence of consecutive blocks on chain ii extending 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,π​(i))\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,\pi(i)), each of which pjp_{j} has DA-voted for. We refer to ε\varepsilon as the vote’s extensions; note that extensions are anchored at the vote’s reported position, not at the proposed tip.141414This is what makes the frontier leader-proof: if the leader’s entries for chain ii are junk or stale, correct voters report a lower position and attach the chain’s true recent blocks as extensions from there.

The endorsed tip of a vote, for chain ii, is the last block specified by ε​(i)\varepsilon(i) if ε​(i)≠λ\varepsilon(i)\neq\lambda, and 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,π​(i))\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,\pi(i)) otherwise. We say a vote counts for a transaction block bb if bb is an ancestor of, or equal to, the vote’s endorsed tip on bb’s chain. (Thus a vote counts for every block on the path it endorses, however that path is split between positions and extensions.) The extraction rules below are stated in terms of this relation.

Standard votes, deviations, and tallies.

Fix a leader block ℓ\ell and a reference extension vector E∗E^{*} (a value of the same type as ε\varepsilon). Recalling that mim_{i} denotes the number of payload entries that ℓ\ell’s chain proposal makes for chain ii (so that π​(i)=mi\pi(i)=m_{i} expresses full support for the proposed tip), a vote for ℓ\ell is standard (w.r.t. E∗E^{*}) if π​(i)=mi\pi(i)=m_{i} for every ii and ε=E∗\varepsilon=E^{*}. The deviation record of a vote is the list of pairs (i,π​(i))(i,\pi(i)) for those chains with π​(i)<mi\pi(i)<m_{i}, together with ε\varepsilon if ε≠E∗\varepsilon\neq E^{*}. A tally for ℓ\ell is a tuple T=(E∗,P,D)T=(E^{*},P,D), where PP is a set of processor indices and DD assigns deviation records to some subset of PP. The tally describes one vote for ℓ\ell per processor in PP: standard w.r.t. E∗E^{*} for processors outside the domain of DD, and otherwise as given by DD. The QCs below consist of a leader block, a tally, and an aggregate signature (plus, for V-QCs, records of the quorum members not voting for ℓ\ell). In the good case (synchrony, all processors correct, no block still in flight at the vote event) all votes are standard w.r.t. a single E∗E^{*}, so DD is empty and all constituent signatures are on a single common message: verification requires one pairing computation. Each deviating vote adds its deviation record and one message to the aggregate, and the worst case is bounded by the quorum size.151515Deviation records may in turn be compressed, e.g. by recording only the coordinates at which a deviating extension vector differs from E∗E^{*}, and by sharing identical records across voters; we do not specify this further. A Raptr-style scheme of per-position keys, under which position deviations would not fragment the aggregate, does not pay here: extensions cannot be keyed, ranging as they do over arbitrary hash values, and extensions concern precisely the blocks racing the vote event, which is where benign disagreement concentrates.

The functions 𝖯𝗈𝗌𝗂𝗍𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)\mathsf{Positions}(\mathcal{S},\ell) and 𝖤𝗑𝗍𝖾𝗇𝗌𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)\mathsf{Extensions}(\mathcal{S},\ell).

Used by pjp_{j} to form its vote for ℓ=(v,H​(Q),C)\ell=(v,H(Q),C). 𝖯𝗈𝗌𝗂𝗍𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)\mathsf{Positions}(\mathcal{S},\ell) maps each ii to the greatest k≤mik\leq m_{i} such that pjp_{j} has DA-voted for 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,k′)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k^{\prime}) for all k′∈[1,k]k^{\prime}\in[1,k]. 𝖤𝗑𝗍𝖾𝗇𝗌𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)\mathsf{Extensions}(\mathcal{S},\ell) maps each ii to the longest sequence of payloads (H(b1.Tr),…,H(bm.Tr))(H(b^{1}.\mathrm{Tr}),\dots,H(b^{m}.\mathrm{Tr})) with m≤em\leq e such that b1,…,bmb^{1},\dots,b^{m} are blocks on chain ii that pjp_{j} has DA-voted for, with b1b^{1}’s parent the block 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,𝖯𝗈𝗌𝗂𝗍𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)​(i))\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,\mathsf{Positions}(\mathcal{S},\ell)(i)) and bkb^{k} the parent of bk+1b^{k+1} for each k<mk<m (and to λ\lambda if there is no such sequence).

Novote and nullify messages.

For v∈ℕ≥1v\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}, a novote(vv) message by pjp_{j} is a message (novote,v,s)(\mathrm{novote},v,s) with ss pjp_{j}’s ordinary signature on (novote,v)(\mathrm{novote},v), and a nullify(vv) message by pjp_{j} is a message (nullify,v,ρ)(\mathrm{nullify},v,\rho) with ρ\rho pjp_{j}’s (2​f+1)(2f+1)-threshold share on (nullify,v)(\mathrm{nullify},v). A correct processor that times out in view vv without voting sends both, while a correct processor that nullifies view vv after voting (see Algorithm 4.2, lines 16–19) sends only the latter. Correct processors never send both a vote for a view vv leader block and a novote(vv) message.161616This property is what separates V-QCs (which certify how far each chain may safely be extended) from mere view progression, and the analysis relies on it. It is the reason novote and nullify are distinct message types, and the reason the former is an ordinary signature (novotes appear individually attributed inside V-QCs) while the latter is a threshold share (nullifications need certify nothing about who nullified).

Nullifications.

A nullification for view vv is a message (nullification,v,τ)(\mathrm{nullification},v,\tau), where τ\tau is the (2​f+1)(2f+1)-threshold signature on (nullify,v)(\mathrm{nullify},v), formed from the shares of nullify(vv) messages by 2​f+12f+1 different processors. (A nullification is thus of constant size, and self-describing: it specifies the view it nullifies and what τ\tau is a signature on. The tag also syntactically distinguishes nullifications from nullify(vv) messages, whose shares are group elements of the same kind as τ\tau.)

L-QCs.

An L-QC for the leader block ℓ\ell is a tuple

(ℓ,T,s),(\ell,\,T,\,s),

where T=(E∗,P,D)T=(E^{*},P,D) is a tally for ℓ\ell with |P|=n−f|P|=n-f, and ss is the aggregate of the signatures of the n−fn-f votes described by TT. An L-QC thus certifies a set of n−fn-f votes for ℓ\ell by distinct processors, and we identify it with that set.

V-QCs.

A V-QC for view vv is a tuple

Q=(ℓ,T,N,X,s),Q=(\ell,\,T,\,N,\,X,\,s),

certifying a set WW of n−fn-f view vv messages by distinct processors, where, writing CC for the chain proposal of ℓ\ell:

  • •

    T=(E∗,P,D)T=(E^{*},P,D) is a tally for ℓ\ell with |P|≥2​f+1|P|\geq 2f+1; the votes it describes are referred to as the votes for CC in WW;

  • •

    NN is a set of processor indices, each contributing a novote(vv) message to WW;

  • •

    XX assigns, to some further set of processor indices, records determining complete votes (v,H​(ℓ′),π,ε)(v,H(\ell^{\prime}),\pi,\varepsilon) for other view vv leader blocks ℓ′\ell^{\prime},171717Votes for other leader blocks can exist only if 𝗅𝖾𝖺𝖽​(v)\mathsf{lead}(v) equivocates, in which case any two such blocks, being signed, are evidence of misbehaviour. Note that the records in XX determine such votes in full: per the atomicity footnote above, a QC’s record of a vote (however succinctly encoded) must always determine the vote’s complete content. and;

  • •

    ss is the aggregate of the signatures of all messages in WW (the novotes contributing a single common message to the aggregate).

The sets PP and NN and the domain of XX are disjoint, with sizes summing to n−fn-f. We write Q.viewQ.\mathrm{view} for vv, and identify QQ with the pair (W,C)(W,C). There is a distinguished initial V-QC QgenQ_{\mathrm{gen}} for view 0, considered received by all processors at the start of the execution, with 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Qgen)i:=bgeni\mathsf{Tips}(Q_{\mathrm{gen}})_{i}:=b_{\mathrm{gen}}^{i} for each ii.

The function 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q).

Defined for any V-QC Q=(W,C)Q=(W,C), the value 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q) maps each chain ii to a transaction block, and is thought of as specifying, for each chain, a tip that is safe to extend given QQ. For each chain ii, let ViV_{i} be the votes for CC in WW (so |Vi|≥2​f+1|V_{i}|\geq 2f+1), and proceed as follows.

  • •

    Positions. Order the values {π​(i):π∈Vi}\{\pi(i):\pi\in V_{i}\} from greatest to least (with multiplicity), discard the first ff, and let kik_{i} be the next value. Set bi:=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki)b_{i}:=\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k_{i}).

  • •

    Extension carry. Redefine bib_{i} to be a deepest block on chain ii that extends bib_{i} and that at least 2​f+12f+1 votes in ViV_{i} count for, if there is one, choosing deterministically (say, by least hash) if there is more than one.181818For n=5​f+1n=5f+1 the choice never arises: two incompatible candidates would each require 2​f+12f+1 supporting votes, no vote counts for both, and |Vi|≤n−f=4​f+1|V_{i}|\leq n-f=4f+1. For larger nn it may arise, but any deterministic choice is safe. To see this, suppose an extension block tt on chain ii is finalised by some same-view L-QC: all n−fn-f of that L-QC’s votes count for tt, so at least n−2​fn-2f correct processors do, of which at least n−3​f≥2​f+1n-3f\geq 2f+1 appear in ViV_{i}; meanwhile any block incompatible with tt has at most ff correct supporters, so muster at most 2​f2f votes. Every candidate here is thus compatible with tt, and every deepest candidate (being at least as deep as tt, which itself qualifies) extends tt.

Then 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i:=bi\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i}:=b_{i}. Since anchors specify bases explicitly, each 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i} is given as an explicit (hash, height) pair by QQ alone: no other V-QC is needed to interpret it. Note also that each coordinate of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q) has been DA-voted by at least one correct processor (at least f+1f+1 when the extension carry applies), which therefore possesses the block and all of its ancestors down to a DA-certified block. This secures data availability for all blocks entering the total ordering defined below, quantified precisely by the availability lemma of Section 5.

The function 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q).

Defined for any L-QC QQ for the leader block ℓ=(v,H​(Q′),C)\ell=(v,H(Q^{\prime}),C), the value 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q) maps each chain ii to a transaction block, and is thought of as specifying, for each chain, the tip finalised by QQ. For each chain ii, proceed as follows.

  • •

    Positions. Order the values {π​(i)}\{\pi(i)\} over the n−fn-f votes in QQ from greatest to least (with multiplicity), discard the first 3​f3f, and let ki∗k^{*}_{i} be the next value. Set bi∗:=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki∗)b^{*}_{i}:=\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k^{*}_{i}).

  • •

    Extensions. If ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i}, redefine bi∗b^{*}_{i} to be the deepest block on chain ii that extends bi∗b^{*}_{i} and that every vote in QQ counts for, if there is one. (If ki∗<mik^{*}_{i}<m_{i}, the extension step does not apply.)

Then 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)i:=bi∗\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{i}:=b^{*}_{i}. Note the asymmetry of thresholds: positions use the rank rules (discard ff, respectively 3​f3f), while extensions use support thresholds (2​f+12f+1, respectively unanimity above a fully supported proposal path). One might hope to treat both by a single rank rule, counting extension depths along with positions. The rank rules are sound precisely because the proposal pins one block per position, so votes on a chain’s positions lie on a common path and a rank determines a block. Extensions lie above anything pinned. Under an equivocating producer, votes may split between incompatible branches, a rank then determines only a height, and the branch-aware repair at the same thresholds is impossible; whence the strengthened thresholds, which are forced at n=5​f+1n=5f+1.191919Quorum intersection gives that 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′′)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime\prime})_{i} extends 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{i} for every V-QC Q′′Q^{\prime\prime} of the same view (Lemma 7). For positions: at least 3​f+13f+1 of QQ’s votes report positions ≥ki∗\geq k^{*}_{i}, so at least f+1f+1 of them, from correct voters, appear in the tally of Q′′Q^{\prime\prime}, whence Q′′Q^{\prime\prime}’s rank is at least ki∗k^{*}_{i}. For extensions: ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i} pins Q′′Q^{\prime\prime}’s rank at mim_{i} exactly, and at least n−3​f≥2​f+1n-3f\geq 2f+1 of the votes counting for 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{i} appear in Q′′Q^{\prime\prime}’s tally, forcing the carry; any block incompatible with 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{i} musters at most 2​f2f votes, so every carry candidate extends it. The condition ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i} cannot be dropped, since without it an equivocating producer can arrange one execution finalising an extension block on one branch, another finalising a proposed entry on the other, with a single V-QC common to both, so that no extraction rule applied to that V-QC is safe in both executions. Below unanimity this fails for n=5​f+1n=5f+1: for any finalisation threshold less than n−fn-f, one can construct two executions sharing a V-QC bit-for-bit in which incompatible extensions reach the threshold, so that no extraction rule applied to V-QCs is safe in both (Section 5, where Theorem 4 determines the exact threshold, ⌈(n+3​f)/2⌉\lceil(n+3f)/2\rceil, for every n≥5​f+1n\geq 5f+1). (Guarantees short of a place in the total ordering are available at weaker thresholds: see the block inclusion theorem of Section 5.)

The total ordering.

Suppose TT maps each chain to a transaction block on that chain. The positions above TT are the pairs (o,i)(o,i), for offsets o≥1o\geq 1 and chains 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n; position (o,i)(o,i) refers to height Ti.height+oT_{i}.\mathrm{height}+o on chain ii. The horizontal order on these positions is lexicographic with offset taken first: (o,i)(o,i) precedes (o′,i′)(o^{\prime},i^{\prime}) if o<o′o<o^{\prime}, or if o=o′o=o^{\prime} and i<i′i<i^{\prime}. (So the positions at offset 11 come first, ordered by chain index, then those at offset 22, and so on.) If T′T^{\prime} also maps chains to blocks, then 𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(T,T′)\mathsf{Horiz}(T,T^{\prime}) denotes the sequence of blocks obtained by visiting the positions above TT in horizontal order and appending, at each position whose height is at most Ti′.heightT^{\prime}_{i}.\mathrm{height} on its chain ii, the ancestor of Ti′T^{\prime}_{i} at that height. (In the intended case Ti′T^{\prime}_{i} extends TiT_{i}; the definition does not require this, however, and when a proposal’s anchor jumps to a DA-certificate on a branch incompatible with TiT_{i} — possible only under an equivocating producer — the appended blocks are simply read off Ti′T^{\prime}_{i}’s own path.) Thus every chain’s first new block is appended before any chain’s second. Note that, for each ii, every block on Ti′T^{\prime}_{i}’s path above height Ti.heightT_{i}.\mathrm{height} appears in the sequence: the definition determines only how the chains are interleaved, never which blocks are included.202020This is the horizontal ordering; heights are measured relative to each chain’s previous tip. Alternatives (vertical, hybrid, leader-scheduled) can be substituted without affecting the analysis, provided the ordering is a deterministic function of (T,T′)(T,T^{\prime}). Each V-QC QQ then specifies a sequence 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q)\mathsf{Ord}(Q) of transaction blocks, defined recursively: 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Qgen):=λ\mathsf{Ord}(Q_{\mathrm{gen}}):=\lambda and, where Q=(W,C)Q=(W,C) is a V-QC for the leader block ℓ=(v,H​(Q′),C)\ell=(v,H(Q^{\prime}),C),

𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q):=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)⌢​𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)).\mathsf{Ord}(Q):=\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime})^{\frown}\mathsf{Horiz}\bigl(\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime}),\mathsf{Tips}(Q)\bigr).

Similarly, each L-QC QQ for ℓ=(v,H​(Q′),C)\ell=(v,H(Q^{\prime}),C) specifies a sequence

𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(Q):=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)⌢​ρ,\mathsf{Emit}(Q):=\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime})^{\frown}\rho,

defined as follows. Say chain jj is settled (w.r.t. QQ) if kj∗=mjk^{*}_{j}=m_{j} and no vote in QQ counts for any block strictly extending 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j}; otherwise jj is unsettled.212121If jj is settled, then no V-QC for the view can specify a tip for chain jj beyond 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j}. Positions cannot advance, being capped at the proposed tip, an ancestor of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j} (or equal to it). An extension carry beyond 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j} would require 2​f+12f+1 votes counting for a block beyond, hence at least f+1f+1 correct ones, while no vote in QQ counts for such a block and at most ff correct votes lie outside QQ. The condition kj∗=mjk^{*}_{j}=m_{j} cannot be dropped, since below the proposed tip a V-QC’s tip advances at the threshold f+1f+1, which ff faulty votes and a single correct vote from outside QQ can meet, and no L-QC can certify that the latter does not exist. An unsettled chain may gain blocks above 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j} in the eventual ordering, and blocks so gained would precede, in the horizontal sweep, blocks of other chains at greater offsets. This is why emission must halt at an unsettled chain’s frontier. Note that a chain’s potential growth is in any case bounded: no vote endorses blocks more than ee beyond its reported position, so the sweep’s lookahead for an unsettled chain is capped at ee beyond the deepest endorsed block: chains are never ‘potentially infinite’. To form ρ\rho, visit the positions above 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′)\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime}) in horizontal order and, at each position, on chain jj say, act as follows:

  • •

    if the position’s height is at most that of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j}, append the ancestor of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)_{j} at that height;

  • •

    otherwise, if chain jj is settled, append nothing and continue;

  • •

    otherwise, halt.

Then ρ\rho is the sequence of blocks appended before the halt. If every chain is settled, no halt ever occurs and ρ\rho is the whole of 𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗​(Q))\mathsf{Horiz}(\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime}),\mathsf{Tips}^{*}(Q)). In the good case, the entire total ordering, extensions included, is emitted upon receipt of a single L-QC (‘entire’ meaning through the deepest blocks the voters had received when they voted). The sequence of transactions corresponding to 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(Q)\mathsf{Emit}(Q) (concatenating the values b.Trb.\mathrm{Tr} in order, removing duplicates) is what a processor appends to its log upon receiving the L-QC QQ. The analysis establishes that 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(Q)⪯𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′′)\mathsf{Emit}(Q)\preceq\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime\prime}) for any V-QC Q′′Q^{\prime\prime} of the same view, so that logs remain consistent as later views extend the ordering.

Finalisation from the vote pool.

Since any n−fn-f votes for ℓ\ell form an L-QC, a processor holding a pool PP of at least n−fn-f votes for ℓ\ell, by distinct processors (a faulty processor may sign more than one vote for ℓ\ell; the pool retains at most one), need never enumerate L-QCs. The rules below apply to PP directly, and it is these that the analysis of Section 5 treats, with an L-QC’s rules as the special case |P|=n−f|P|=n-f; they dominate the rules for every individual L-QC assemblable from PP, and settledness from a pool is strictly more permissive than from any single L-QC, so pooling can emit strictly more. Define 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P):=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)⌢​ρ\mathsf{Emit}(P):=\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime})^{\frown}\rho exactly as for L-QCs, but with the following in place of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗\mathsf{Tips}^{*} and settledness, for each chain ii:

  • •

    Positions. ki∗k^{*}_{i} is the (3​f+1)(3f+1)-th largest value π​(i)\pi(i) over the votes in PP (this is the drop-3​f3f rule applied to the best n−fn-f votes for chain ii);

  • •

    Extensions. If ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i}, then FiF_{i} is the deepest block extending 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,mi)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,m_{i}) that at least n−fn-f votes in PP count for (or 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,mi)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,m_{i}) itself if there is none). If ki∗<mik^{*}_{i}<m_{i}, then Fi:=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki∗)F_{i}:=\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k^{*}_{i});

  • •

    Settledness. Chain ii is settled if ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i} and βi+(n−|P|)≤f\beta_{i}+(n-|P|)\leq f, where βi\beta_{i} is the number of votes in PP counting for some block strictly extending FiF_{i}.

The settledness condition generalises the L-QC rule (to which it reduces when |P|=n−f|P|=n-f). It ensures that at most ff correct votes counting beyond FiF_{i} can exist at all, seen or unseen, so no V-QC can carry chain ii past FiF_{i}. Emission is monotone, since as votes arrive each quantity above only improves, and successive values of 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) (like the values 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(Q)\mathsf{Emit}(Q) for the various L-QCs assemblable from PP, all of which 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) dominates) are prefixes of one common sequence, so a processor may re-emit as its pool grows.

The function 𝖲𝖾𝗅𝖾𝖼𝗍𝖠𝗇𝖼𝗁𝗈𝗋​(𝒮,v)\mathsf{SelectAnchor}(\mathcal{S},v).

Used by the leader of view vv to select the V-QC to build on. If v′<vv^{\prime}<v is the greatest view such that 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a V-QC for view v′v^{\prime}, the function outputs the lexicographically least V-QC for view v′v^{\prime} contained in 𝒮\mathcal{S}.

The procedure 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉𝗈𝗌𝖾𝖢𝗁𝖺𝗂𝗇𝗌​(Q,v)\mathsf{ProposeChains}(Q,v).

Executed by the leader pip_{i} of view vv to determine a new leader block. To execute the procedure, pip_{i} forms the chain proposal CC as follows, for each chain jj: let b:=𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)jb:=\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{j};

  • •

    if 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a DA-certificate for a block on chain jj of height greater than b.heightb.\mathrm{height}, then aja_{j} is such a certificate of greatest height; otherwise aj:=(H(b),b.height)a_{j}:=(H(b),b.\mathrm{height});

  • •

    xjx_{j} is the longest sequence of payloads (H(b1.Tr),…,H(bm.Tr))(H(b^{1}.\mathrm{Tr}),\dots,H(b^{m}.\mathrm{Tr})), m≤dm\leq d, such that b1,…,bmb^{1},\dots,b^{m} are blocks on chain jj that pip_{i} has DA-voted for, with b1b^{1}’s parent the base and bkb^{k} the parent of bk+1b^{k+1} for k<mk<m.

Then pip_{i} disseminates the leader block (v,H​(Q),C)(v,H(Q),C), together with the V-QC QQ itself (whether or not QQ was previously forwarded), so that every processor receiving the block also receives the exact V-QC it references.222222This dissemination is necessary, not merely convenient: the forwarding rule below sends each processor at most one V-QC per view, chosen when the view’s first V-QC appears, while 𝖲𝖾𝗅𝖾𝖼𝗍𝖠𝗇𝖼𝗁𝗈𝗋\mathsf{SelectAnchor} returns the lexicographically least V-QC held at proposal time, which may have been assembled later, from votes no one else received. Without this dissemination, a single privately delivered vote could leave the leader referencing an object that no other correct processor holds, and, since proposal validity requires the exact object referenced, no correct processor could vote. The egress cost is the one already accounted for in the forwarding footnote below.

When 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a valid proposal for view vv.

This condition is satisfied when:

  1. (i)

    𝒮\mathcal{S} contains precisely one leader block ℓ\ell of the form ℓ=(v,q,C)\ell=(v,q,C) signed by 𝗅𝖾𝖺𝖽​(v)\mathsf{lead}(v);

  2. (ii)

    𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a V-QC QQ with H​(Q)=qH(Q)=q, for some view v′<vv^{\prime}<v, and CC is well-formed with respect to 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q);232323Well-formedness requires, for each chain jj: either aj=(H(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌(Q)j),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌(Q)j.height)a_{j}=(H(\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{j}),\,\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{j}.\mathrm{height}), or aja_{j} is a valid DA-certificate for chain jj of height greater than that of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)j\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{j}; and |xj|≤d|x_{j}|\leq d. Note that 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q) is computable from QQ alone, so this condition is checkable given ℓ\ell and the referenced V-QC. Parent-links among proposed blocks hold by construction (entries are payloads); voters do not verify that the specified blocks exist, and simply report a lower position when they have not DA-voted them. and;

  3. (iii)

    𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a nullification for each view in the open interval (v′,v)(v^{\prime},v).

When (i)–(iii) are satisfied w.r.t. ℓ\ell, we say 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a valid proposal ℓ\ell for view vv. Note that this condition guards only a processor’s first route to voting (line 8 of Algorithm 4.2). A processor may also vote upon receiving a V-QC for the current view (lines 12–13), without checking validity. In this case, the V-QC’s 2​f+12f+1 votes for the designated proposal ensure that at least f+1f+1 correct processors found it valid, and the V-QC contains everything needed to form the vote (it contains ℓ\ell, which determines H​(ℓ)H(\ell), and 𝖯𝗈𝗌𝗂𝗍𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌\mathsf{Positions} and 𝖤𝗑𝗍𝖾𝗇𝗌𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌\mathsf{Extensions} require only CC and the voter’s own DA-voting history).

Further local variables.

The variable 𝚟\mathtt{v} (initially 11) specifies the present view. The local timer 𝚃\mathtt{T} (initially 0) increments in real time and is reset upon entering each view. The variables 𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍\mathtt{nullified}, 𝚙𝚛𝚘𝚙𝚘𝚜𝚎𝚍\mathtt{proposed} (initially false\mathrm{false}) and 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍\mathtt{notarised} (initially ⊥\bot) record whether pip_{i} has sent a nullify(𝚟\mathtt{v}) message, whether it has proposed a leader block for view 𝚟\mathtt{v}, and the leader block it has voted for in the present view; all are reset upon entering a new view.

New nullifications and V-QCs.

As in Minimmit, processors forward all newly received or assembled nullifications and V-QCs to all. At timeslot tt, pip_{i} regards a nullification for view vv as new if 𝒮\mathcal{S} did not contain one for view vv, nor shares forming one, at any smaller timeslot (since threshold signatures are unique, no tie-breaking rule is needed), and regards a V-QC for view vv as new if 𝒮\mathcal{S} contained no V-QC for view vv at any smaller timeslot, forwarding the lexicographically least V-QC for view vv that 𝒮\mathcal{S} then contains.242424Unlike Minimmit’s M-notarisations, V-QCs are not constant-size (Section 3.8), but forwarding them is unalarming. In terms of egress, note that under standard operation the leader of the next view in any case sends both the V-QC (in disseminating the V-QC it references, per 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉𝗈𝗌𝖾𝖢𝗁𝖺𝗂𝗇𝗌\mathsf{ProposeChains}) and its own leader block. Each other processor’s forwarding duty, a single V-QC to all, is therefore less than the per-view egress the protocol already demands of each leader. Moreover, in the common case a processor forwards at a moment when it has nothing else to send, and nothing in the protocol waits on the transmission, so the cost is bandwidth off the critical path. In terms of ingress, a processor already holding the V-QC need not attend to more than a brief identifier at the head of the message.

Walk-through: lines 16–19 of Algorithm 4.2 ensure view progression.

Section 3 asked the reader to take on trust that every view produces a V-notarisation or a nullification; lines 16–19, inherited from Minimmit, are the delicate part of the mechanism, and we now explain them. The concern is a correct processor that has voted in view 𝚟\mathtt{v} but sees neither a V-QC nor a nullification form. Perhaps the leader equivocated and votes are split, or other processors timed out before the proposal reached them. Waiting indefinitely is not an option, but nor may the processor simply nullify, since a nullification must prove that no view 𝚟\mathtt{v} block receives an L-notarisation, and the processor’s own vote may be helping some block towards exactly that. The rule resolves the tension: the processor nullifies only upon receiving, from 2​f+12f+1 distinct processors, messages none of which support the block ℓ\ell it voted for (nullify or novote messages, or votes for other blocks). At least f+1f+1 of these come from correct processors and, considering the first correct supporter of any given block to nullify in this way, one can check that none of those correct processors ever votes for ℓ\ell, capping its support at n−f−1n-f-1, so nullifying is safe. Conversely, the rule ensures progression. After GST, every correct processor eventually holds a view 𝚟\mathtt{v} message from every correct processor. If 2​f+12f+1 votes for a single block are among them, a V-notarisation exists, and otherwise every correct voter eventually accumulates 2​f+12f+1 messages of the stated forms and nullifies, so that a nullification forms. Note finally that the processor sends its nullify share without a novote message, since it did vote and a novote would be false. (Full arguments appear in Section 5.)

5 Verification

5.1 Consistency

Following Minimmit, we reason about notarisations: sets of messages actually sent, whether or not any processor assembles the corresponding certificate. Precisely, we say a transaction block bb is certifiable if at least n−2​fn-2f processors send DA-votes for bb; a leader block ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation if at least n−fn-f processors send votes for ℓ\ell; a V-notarisation for view vv is a set WW of view vv votes and novote(vv) messages, one each from n−fn-f distinct processors, at least 2​f+12f+1 of which are votes for a common leader block ℓ\ell, whose proposal WW is said to designate; and view vv receives a nullification if at least 2​f+12f+1 processors send nullify(vv) messages.252525One caution regarding designation: for n=5​f+1n=5f+1 a V-notarisation designates exactly one proposal (two disjoint sets of 2​f+12f+1 votes would require 4​f+2>n−f4f+2>n-f messages), but for larger nn it may designate two. The ambiguity is harmless. A V-QC always names a single designated proposal, that of the leader block it contains, and it is this designation that parenthood (below) and the protocol’s rules consult. Wherever the lemmas below extract values from a V-notarisation (Lemmas 7 and 8), an L-notarisation for the view is in force, and Lemma 4 then makes the designation unique. Any QC certifies a notarisation of the corresponding kind (this uses the assumption that signatures cannot be forged), and the functions 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌\mathsf{Tips}, 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗\mathsf{Tips}^{*}, 𝖮𝗋𝖽\mathsf{Ord} and 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍\mathsf{Emit} depend only on the underlying notarisation and the designated proposal, so all statements below transfer to QCs. Recall from Section 2 that a message received at timeslot tt was sent at a timeslot strictly before tt.

We begin with the chain layer.

Lemma 1 (Certified blocks are compatible).

Any two certifiable transaction blocks on the same chain are compatible.

Proof.

Towards a contradiction, suppose otherwise. Among all pairs of incompatible certifiable blocks (on some fixed chain), choose a pair b,b′b,b^{\prime}, of heights h≤h′h\leq h^{\prime}, so that (h,h′)(h,h^{\prime}) is lexicographically minimal. Each of b,b′b,b^{\prime} has DA-votes from n−2​fn-2f distinct processors. The two voter sets intersect in at least 2​(n−2​f)−n=n−4​f≥f+12(n-2f)-n=n-4f\geq f+1 processors, so some correct processor pp must DA-vote for both. If h=h′h=h^{\prime} this contradicts condition (i) for DA-voting (one DA-vote per chain and height), so h<h′h<h^{\prime}.

Consider the timeslot at which pp sent its DA-vote for b′b^{\prime}, and let cc, of height h′′<h′h^{\prime\prime}<h^{\prime}, be the anchoring certificate at that vote (so that h′′h^{\prime\prime} is the greatest certified height below h′h^{\prime} in pp’s local value 𝒮\mathcal{S} at that timeslot). By condition (iii), pp then held blocks bh′′+1,…,bh′=b′b_{h^{\prime\prime}+1},\dots,b_{h^{\prime}}=b^{\prime} forming the path from cc to b′b^{\prime}.

First, suppose h′′≥hh^{\prime\prime}\geq h. The block cc is certifiable, and the pair b,cb,c has both heights below h′h^{\prime}. It follows from our choice of (h,h′)(h,h^{\prime}) that the blocks bb and cc are compatible. Then bb is an ancestor of cc, hence of b′b^{\prime}: a contradiction.

So h′′<hh^{\prime\prime}<h, and we may set zz to be the block on the path from cc to b′b^{\prime} of height hh. Since bb and b′b^{\prime} are incompatible, bb and zz are incompatible; in particular z≠bz\neq b. By condition (iii), pp sent a DA-vote for zz at or before the timeslot at which it voted for b′b^{\prime}. Since pp votes for bb, this means pp DA-votes at height hh for two distinct blocks, contradicting condition (i). ∎

We next turn to the consensus layer.

Lemma 2 (One vote per view).

A correct processor sends at most one vote for each view.

Proof.

Votes are sent only at lines 7–8 and 12–13 of Algorithm 4.2, both guarded by 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍=⊥\mathtt{notarised}=\bot; voting sets 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍\mathtt{notarised} to the block voted for, and the variable is reset only upon entering a new view. ∎

Lemma 3 (Vote–novote exclusivity).

No correct processor sends both a vote for a view vv leader block and a novote(vv) message.

Proof.

Novote messages are sent only at line 10, guarded (at line 9) by 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍=⊥\mathtt{notarised}=\bot and 𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍=false\mathtt{nullified}=\mathrm{false}. A prior vote in the view sets 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍≠⊥\mathtt{notarised}\neq\bot, blocking line 10; a prior novote sets 𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍=true\mathtt{nullified}=\mathrm{true}, blocking both voting guards for the remainder of the view. ∎

Lemma 4 (Designation).

Suppose the view vv leader block ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation. Then at most 2​f2f processors ever send view vv votes for leader blocks other than ℓ\ell. In particular, every view vv V-notarisation designates ℓ\ell’s proposal, and no other view vv leader block receives 2​f+12f+1 votes.

Proof.

At least n−2​fn-2f of the n−fn-f processors voting for ℓ\ell are correct and, by Lemma 2, send no other view vv vote. Any view vv vote for another block is therefore sent by one of the remaining at most 2​f2f processors. ∎

Lemma 5 (No nullification).

Suppose the view vv leader block ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation. Then view vv receives no nullification.

Proof.

Let AA be the set of correct processors that vote for ℓ\ell and BB the set of remaining correct processors. Where fa≤ff_{a}\leq f is the number of faulty processors, |A|≥n−f−fa|A|\geq n-f-f_{a}, so |B|≤(n−fa)−(n−f−fa)=f|B|\leq(n-f_{a})-(n-f-f_{a})=f.

We claim no member of AA ever sends nullify(vv). A member of AA has 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍≠⊥\mathtt{notarised}\neq\bot for the remainder of the view, so can send nullify(vv) only via lines 16–19, upon holding 2​f+12f+1 messages by distinct processors, each a nullify(vv), a novote(vv), or a view vv vote for a block other than ℓ\ell. Towards a contradiction, suppose there is some least timeslot tt at which some p∈Ap\in A does so. Each of pp’s 2​f+12f+1 evidence messages was sent strictly before tt. Consider any correct sender among them: a novote(vv) sender lies in BB by Lemma 3; the sender of a vote for a block other than ℓ\ell lies in BB by Lemma 2; and a nullify(vv) sender lies in BB, or else is a member of AA that sent nullify(vv) strictly before tt, contradicting the minimality of tt. So the correct senders all lie in BB, and number at most ff. With at most ff faulty senders, the evidence totals at most 2​f<2​f+12f<2f+1: a contradiction.

Correct nullify(vv) senders therefore all lie in BB. With at most ff faulty processors, fewer than 2​f+12f+1 processors send nullify(vv) messages, and view vv receives no nullification. ∎

Next, we establish consistency of the leader chain itself. Define the parent of a leader block ℓ=(v,H​(Q),C)\ell=(v,H(Q),C) to be the leader block that QQ contains (and define the parent of any leader block referencing QgenQ_{\mathrm{gen}} to be ℓgen\ell_{\mathrm{gen}}). Ancestry and compatibility for leader blocks are then defined as for transaction blocks.

Lemma 6 (The leader chain).

Suppose the view vv leader block ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation. Then every leader block receiving 2​f+12f+1 votes in any view w≥vw\geq v has ℓ\ell as an ancestor. In particular, leader blocks receiving L-notarisations are pairwise compatible.

Proof.

By induction on ww. For w=vw=v the claim is Lemma 4. So let w>vw>v, suppose the claim holds for all views in [v,w)[v,w), and let ℓ′=(w,H​(Q′),C′)\ell^{\prime}=(w,H(Q^{\prime}),C^{\prime}) receive 2​f+12f+1 votes, at least f+1f+1 of them from correct processors. Let qq be a correct processor voting for ℓ′\ell^{\prime} at the earliest timeslot, tqt_{q} say. If qq voted via lines 12–13, its 𝒮\mathcal{S} contained a V-QC for view ww itself, designating ℓ′\ell^{\prime}’s proposal. (This rule fires only upon a V-QC for the processor’s current view; this is not the earlier-view V-QC Q′Q^{\prime} that ℓ′\ell^{\prime} references, which belongs to the line 8 route below.) Such a V-QC certifies 2​f+12f+1 view ww votes for ℓ′\ell^{\prime}, at least f+1f+1 of them correct, all sent strictly before tqt_{q}. This contradicts the choice of qq. So qq voted via lines 7–8, and its 𝒮\mathcal{S} contained a valid proposal, in particular the V-QC Q′Q^{\prime}, for some view u<wu<w, together with a nullification for every view in the open interval (u,w)(u,w). A nullification for a view exists only if that view receives one (2​f+12f+1 shares are needed to form the threshold signature, and shares by correct processors cannot be forged), so by Lemma 5 we have v∉(u,w)v\notin(u,w), i.e. u≥vu\geq v. Now the tally of Q′Q^{\prime} certifies 2​f+12f+1 view uu votes for ℓ′\ell^{\prime}’s parent ℓ′′\ell^{\prime\prime}, which therefore receives 2​f+12f+1 votes in view u∈[v,w)u\in[v,w). By the induction hypothesis (or by Lemma 4 if u=vu=v), ℓ\ell is an ancestor of ℓ′′\ell^{\prime\prime}, hence of ℓ′\ell^{\prime}.

For the final claim, if ℓ\ell and ℓ′\ell^{\prime} receive L-notarisations in views v≤wv\leq w, then ℓ′\ell^{\prime} in particular receives 2​f+12f+1 votes, so has ℓ\ell as an ancestor. ∎

We state the next lemma for pools. Taking PP to be the votes of an L-QC recovers the statement for 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌∗\mathsf{Tips}^{*}.

Lemma 7 (Safe extension).

Let the leader block ℓ=(v,H​(Q),C)\ell=(v,H(Q),C) receive an L-notarisation, let PP be a set of votes for ℓ\ell by at least n−fn-f distinct processors, and let ki∗k^{*}_{i}, FiF_{i} and settledness be as in ‘Finalisation from the vote pool’ (Section 4). Let WW be any view vv V-notarisation. Then, for every chain ii:

  1. (a)

    𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} extends FiF_{i}, and;

  2. (b)

    if chain ii is settled w.r.t. PP, then 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i=Fi\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i}=F_{i}.

Proof.

By Lemma 4, WW designates ℓ\ell’s proposal, so 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)\mathsf{Tips}(W) is computed from the tally ViV_{i} of WW’s votes for ℓ\ell, relative to the same chain proposal CC. A correct processor appearing in WW appears with its unique actual vote, in ViV_{i} if it voted for ℓ\ell (in that case it cannot contribute a novote by Lemma 3, nor a vote for another block by Lemma 2). Fix a chain ii, and let fa≤ff_{a}\leq f be the number of faulty processors.

Positions. By definition of ki∗k^{*}_{i}, at least 3​f+13f+1 votes in PP, by distinct processors, have π​(i)≥ki∗\pi(i)\geq k^{*}_{i}; at least 2​f+12f+1 of these processors are correct, and at most ff processors have no message in WW, so at least f+1f+1 votes in ViV_{i} have π​(i)≥ki∗\pi(i)\geq k^{*}_{i}. The (f+1)(f+1)-th largest position in ViV_{i} is therefore at least ki∗k^{*}_{i}. Writing kik_{i} for the position rank of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i}, we have ki≥ki∗k_{i}\geq k^{*}_{i}.

Proof of (a). If Fi=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki∗)F_{i}=\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k^{*}_{i}), then the position block 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k_{i}) extends FiF_{i}, and the extension-carry step only ever replaces a block by one extending it, so 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} extends FiF_{i}. Otherwise ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i} and at least n−fn-f votes in PP, by distinct processors, count for FiF_{i}, which strictly extends 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,mi)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,m_{i}). Then ki=mik_{i}=m_{i} (positions are capped at mim_{i}), so the position block is 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,mi)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,m_{i}), an ancestor of FiF_{i}. At least n−f−fan-f-f_{a} of the processors counting for FiF_{i} are correct, and at least n−f−fa−f≥n−3​f≥2​f+1n-f-f_{a}-f\geq n-3f\geq 2f+1 of them appear in ViV_{i}, counting for FiF_{i}, so FiF_{i} is a carry candidate. Moreover every carry candidate is compatible with FiF_{i}: if yy is incompatible with FiF_{i}, then a correct processor counting for yy has DA-voted a block incompatible, at some height, with the one DA-voted by each of the ≥n−f−fa\geq n-f-f_{a} correct processors counting for FiF_{i}, so (correct processors DA-voting once per height) at most (n−fa)−(n−f−fa)=f(n-f_{a})-(n-f-f_{a})=f correct processors count for yy, and yy gains at most f+fa≤2​ff+f_{a}\leq 2f votes in ViV_{i}: below the carry threshold. A deepest candidate is at least as deep as FiF_{i} and compatible with it, so extends it, whichever candidate the tie-breaking rule selects. 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} therefore extends FiF_{i}.

Proof of (b). Suppose chain ii is settled, meaning ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i} and βi+(n−|P|)≤f\beta_{i}+(n-|P|)\leq f. Any correct processor whose vote counts for a block strictly extending FiF_{i} either has its vote in PP (there are at most βi\beta_{i} such) or has no vote in PP (there are at most n−|P|n-|P| such processors), giving at most ff correct processors in all. A carry candidate zz strictly extending FiF_{i} would need 2​f+12f+1 votes in ViV_{i} counting for zz, of which at most ff correct and at most fa≤ff_{a}\leq f faulty exist: impossible. Candidates incompatible with FiF_{i} are excluded as in (a), and positions are capped at mim_{i}, so every candidate, and the position block, is an ancestor of or equal to FiF_{i}. By (a), 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} extends FiF_{i}. Combining, 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i=Fi\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i}=F_{i}. ∎

Lemma 8 (Emission is a prefix).

In the setting of Lemma 7, 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)⪯𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)\mathsf{Emit}(P)\preceq\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime}) for every V-QC Q′Q^{\prime} for view vv. In particular, any two values 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P), 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}) extracted from pools of votes for ℓ\ell (by different processors, or at different times) are compatible.

Proof.

By Lemma 4, the leader block contained in Q′Q^{\prime} is ℓ\ell, so Q′Q^{\prime} references QQ and 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q)⌢​𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′))\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime})=\mathsf{Ord}(Q)^{\frown}\mathsf{Horiz}(\mathsf{Tips}(Q),\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})), while 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q)⌢​ρ\mathsf{Emit}(P)=\mathsf{Ord}(Q)^{\frown}\rho: it suffices to show that ρ⪯𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′))\rho\preceq\mathsf{Horiz}(\mathsf{Tips}(Q),\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})). Note that Lemma 7 applies to Q′Q^{\prime}, taking WW to be the V-notarisation that Q′Q^{\prime} certifies. Both sequences visit the positions above 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q) in horizontal order. Consider any position visited by ρ\rho strictly before its halt (if any), on chain jj say. If the position’s height is at most that of FjF_{j}, then ρ\rho appends the ancestor of FjF_{j} at that height; by Lemma 7(a) this is also the ancestor of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′)j\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})_{j} at that height, which is what 𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′))\mathsf{Horiz}(\mathsf{Tips}(Q),\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})) appends. Otherwise chain jj is settled (else ρ\rho would have halted here) and, by Lemma 7(b), 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′)j=Fj\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})_{j}=F_{j} lies below the position, so both sequences append nothing. The two sequences thus agree at every position up to ρ\rho’s halt, where ρ\rho ends: ρ⪯𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q),𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′))\rho\preceq\mathsf{Horiz}(\mathsf{Tips}(Q),\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})).

For the final claim, note that a V-notarisation for view vv exists: any n−fn-f votes of the L-notarisation received by ℓ\ell form one. Both 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) and 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}) are prefixes of 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q′)\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{\prime}) for a V-QC Q′Q^{\prime} certifying it. ∎

Theorem 1 (Consistency).

If pip_{i} and pjp_{j} are correct then, for any timeslots tt and t′t^{\prime}, logi​(t)\mathrm{log}_{i}(t) and logj​(t′)\mathrm{log}_{j}(t^{\prime}) are compatible.

Proof.

Every value taken by the log of a correct processor is the transaction sequence of 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) for some pool PP of n−fn-f or more votes for a leader block ℓ\ell (lines 21–22 of Algorithm 4.2). In particular ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation. Since prefixes of block sequences yield prefixes of the corresponding deduplicated transaction sequences, it suffices to show that any two such values 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P), 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}), for leader blocks ℓ\ell and ℓ′\ell^{\prime} of views v≤v′v\leq v^{\prime}, are compatible as block sequences.

If v=v′v=v^{\prime} then ℓ′=ℓ\ell^{\prime}=\ell by Lemma 4, and the claim is Lemma 8. So suppose v<v′v<v^{\prime}. By Lemma 6, ℓ\ell is an ancestor of ℓ′\ell^{\prime}. Let ℓ=ℓ0,ℓ1,…,ℓr=ℓ′\ell=\ell_{0},\ell_{1},\dots,\ell_{r}=\ell^{\prime} be the path, and for each s<rs<r let Q(s)Q^{(s)} be the V-QC referenced by ℓs+1\ell_{s+1}, so that Q(s)Q^{(s)} designates the proposal of ℓs\ell_{s}. Then:

  • •

    𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)⪯𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(0))\mathsf{Emit}(P)\preceq\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(0)}), by Lemma 8, since Q(0)Q^{(0)} is a V-QC for view vv;

  • •

    𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(s))⪯𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(s+1))\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(s)})\preceq\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(s+1)}) for each s<r−1s<r-1, since ℓs+1\ell_{s+1}, the leader block contained in Q(s+1)Q^{(s+1)}, references Q(s)Q^{(s)}, so that 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(s+1))\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(s+1)}) extends 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(s))\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(s)}) by definition, and;

  • •

    𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(r−1))⪯𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(r-1)})\preceq\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}), since ℓ′\ell^{\prime} references Q(r−1)Q^{(r-1)} and 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q(r−1))⌢​ρ′\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime})=\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{(r-1)})^{\frown}\rho^{\prime}.

Chaining, 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)⪯𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Emit}(P)\preceq\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}). ∎

5.2 Liveness

Recall from Section 4 that 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains a certificate (a V-QC, L-QC, nullification or DA-certificate) whenever it contains messages from which one can be formed. We add one reading convention: the instructions of Algorithms 4.2 and 4.2 are executed repeatedly within each timeslot, until no instruction applies, so that a processor holding view-advancing triggers for several consecutive views passes through all of them in a single timeslot. Bounds below are stated in terms of δ\delta, the (unknown) least upper bound on message delay after GST (Section 2), wherever possible: a message sent at timeslot tt arrives by max⁡{GST,t}+δ\max\{\mathrm{GST},t\}+\delta, and the known bound Δ≥δ\Delta\geq\delta enters only through the 2​Δ2\Delta timeouts.

Lemma 9 (View synchronisation).

If the first correct processor pp to enter view vv does so at timeslot tt, then every correct processor enters a view ≥v\geq v by max⁡{GST,t}+δ\max\{\mathrm{GST},t\}+\delta.

Proof.

Processor pp passed through every view u<vu<v, so its local value 𝒮\mathcal{S} at tt contains, for each such uu, a nullification or V-QC for uu. For each such uu it has therefore forwarded a nullification or V-QC for uu to all processors at the timeslot ≤t\leq t at which one first became new to it (line 2 of Algorithm 4.2). All of these messages arrive by max⁡{GST,t}+δ\max\{\mathrm{GST},t\}+\delta. A correct processor holding, for every u<vu<v, a nullification or V-QC for uu advances (lines 11 and 14), within the timeslot, to a view ≥v\geq v. ∎

Lemma 10 (View exit).

Suppose the first correct processor to enter view vv does so at timeslot t≥GSTt\geq\mathrm{GST}. Then every correct processor enters a view ≥v+1\geq v+1 by t+2​Δ+3​δt+2\Delta+3\delta.

Proof.

Let t′t^{\prime} be the first timeslot at which a correct processor enters a view ≥v+1\geq v+1 (if ever). If t′≤t+2​Δ+2​δt^{\prime}\leq t+2\Delta+2\delta then, by Lemma 9, we are done. So suppose no correct processor enters a view ≥v+1\geq v+1 by t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta; we show t′≤t+2​Δ+3​δt^{\prime}\leq t+2\Delta+3\delta.

By Lemma 9, every correct processor enters view vv by t+δt+\delta, and, remaining in the view, sends exactly one of the following by t+2​Δ+δt+2\Delta+\delta: a vote (lines 7–8 or 12–13), or, at 2​Δ2\Delta on its local timer, a novote(vv) and nullify(vv) pair (lines 9–10). By t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta, therefore, every correct processor holds a view vv vote or novote from every correct processor, giving at least n−fn-f view vv messages by distinct processors. There are two cases.

Suppose first that at least 2​f+12f+1 correct processors vote for a common leader block ℓ\ell. Then by t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta the 𝒮\mathcal{S} of every correct processor contains a V-QC for view vv (assembled from n−fn-f of the correct messages), and every correct processor enters view v+1v+1 at t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta (lines 11 and 14), a contradiction to our supposition.

Otherwise, every leader block receives at most 2​f2f correct votes. Consider any correct processor pp that voted, for ℓp\ell_{p} say. Of the ≥n−f\geq n-f correct view vv messages that pp holds by t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta, those that are votes for ℓp\ell_{p} number at most 2​f2f, so at least n−3​f≥2​f+1n-3f\geq 2f+1, by distinct processors, are each a nullify(vv), a novote(vv), or a vote for a leader block other than ℓp\ell_{p}. At t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta, pp then sends nullify(vv) via lines 16–19, if it has not already done so. Every correct processor has thus sent nullify(vv) by t+2​Δ+2​δt+2\Delta+2\delta. The shares arrive by t+2​Δ+3​δt+2\Delta+3\delta, every correct processor assembles a nullification, and enters view v+1v+1. ∎

Since the first correct processor to enter view v+1v+1 does so at or after the first correct entry into view vv, an induction gives:

Corollary 1.

Every view is eventually entered by every correct processor.

Lemma 11 (Correct-leader views).

Suppose 𝗅𝖾𝖺𝖽​(v)\mathsf{lead}(v) is correct and the first correct processor to enter view vv does so at timeslot t≥GSTt\geq\mathrm{GST}. Then every correct processor votes for the leader’s block ℓ\ell by t+2​δt+2\delta, so that ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation. By t+3​δt+3\delta every correct processor holds a pool of at least n−fn-f votes for ℓ\ell, so finalises ℓ\ell (lines 21–22) and enters view v+1v+1.

Proof.

By Lemma 9, every correct processor enters view vv by t+δt+\delta. Entry times thus lie in [t,t+δ][t,t+\delta], so no correct processor’s view vv timer reaches 2​Δ2\Delta before t+2​Δt+2\Delta.

Every correct processor holds a valid proposal by t+2​δt+2\delta. The leader enters view vv at some τ≤t+δ\tau\leq t+\delta and immediately proposes (lines 3–5), disseminating ℓ=(v,H​(Q),C)\ell=(v,H(Q),C) for the V-QC QQ returned by 𝖲𝖾𝗅𝖾𝖼𝗍𝖠𝗇𝖼𝗁𝗈𝗋\mathsf{SelectAnchor}, of view v′v^{\prime} say, and ℓ\ell arrives everywhere by τ+δ≤t+2​δ\tau+\delta\leq t+2\delta. Since 𝖲𝖾𝗅𝖾𝖼𝗍𝖠𝗇𝖼𝗁𝗈𝗋\mathsf{SelectAnchor} returns a V-QC for the greatest view for which the leader holds one, the leader advanced through each view u∈(v′,v)u\in(v^{\prime},v) by nullification, and holds a nullification for each. The V-QC QQ is disseminated together with ℓ\ell (see 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉𝗈𝗌𝖾𝖢𝗁𝖺𝗂𝗇𝗌\mathsf{ProposeChains}), so arrives everywhere by τ+δ≤t+2​δ\tau+\delta\leq t+2\delta; each nullification became new to the leader at some timeslot ≤τ\leq\tau and was forwarded to all upon becoming new (line 2, by the leader or by whoever first supplied it), so arrives everywhere by max⁡{GST,τ}+δ≤t+2​δ\max\{\mathrm{GST},\tau\}+\delta\leq t+2\delta (threshold signatures being unique, what was forwarded is the nullification). The leader being correct, ℓ\ell is the unique view vv leader block signed by 𝗅𝖾𝖺𝖽​(v)\mathsf{lead}(v) and CC is well-formed with respect to 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)\mathsf{Tips}(Q): conditions (i)–(iii) of proposal validity hold at every correct processor by t+2​δt+2\delta.

No correct processor sends a novote(vv) or nullify(vv) message. Timeouts (lines 9–10) fire no earlier than t+2​Δ≥t+2​δt+2\Delta\geq t+2\delta, by which time 𝒮\mathcal{S} contains the valid proposal, and lines 6–8 precede lines 9–10 within a timeslot, so a processor reaching 2​Δ2\Delta on its timer votes rather than timing out (its guards hold, as we check below). For nullify(vv) via lines 16–19: consider the first correct processor to send nullify(vv). It has voted, necessarily for ℓ\ell (a vote via lines 7–8 requires a valid proposal, and ℓ\ell is the unique candidate; a vote via lines 12–13 requires a view vv V-QC designating another block, hence f+1f+1 correct votes for that block, which do not exist, by this same argument applied inductively to earlier voters). Its evidence must contain 2​f+12f+1 messages, none supporting ℓ\ell. Correct processors supply no novotes and no earlier nullifies (it is first), and no votes for other blocks, so at most ff faulty messages qualify: the evidence never accumulates.

Every correct processor votes for ℓ\ell by t+2​δt+2\delta. At the first timeslot (≤t+2​δ\leq t+2\delta) at which it holds the valid proposal while in view vv, its guards hold: 𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍=false\mathtt{nullified}=\mathrm{false} since it sends no nullify(vv) (above); 𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚜𝚎𝚍\mathtt{notarised} is ⊥\bot unless it has already voted for ℓ\ell (the unique votable block, as above). It remains to check that it is still in view vv. It cannot have entered v+1v+1 via a nullification for vv (f+1f+1 correct shares would be needed, and none exist), and if via a V-QC for vv, then lines 12–13 fire before line 14, so it voted for ℓ\ell first.

Thus at least n−fn-f correct processors vote for ℓ\ell by t+2​δt+2\delta: an L-notarisation. The votes arrive everywhere by t+3​δt+3\delta, whereupon every correct processor finalises ℓ\ell (lines 21–22) and, holding a V-QC for view vv (any n−fn-f of the votes), enters view v+1v+1. ∎

Lemma 11 is the 3​δ3\delta figure of Section 3.6: in a correct-leader view after GST, the 2​Δ2\Delta timeouts never bind, and every bound is governed by the actual network delay.

Data availability.

One convention remains before the theorem. Recall from Section 2 that we solve Extractable SMR: the protocol guarantees that the data of every block entering the ordering is retrievable, with the retrieval mechanism left to implementation. Note first that 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) is computable without block data: votes, chain proposals and headers determine the emitted sequence of block identifiers. We accordingly read lines 21–22 modulo retrieval: the emitted identifiers are determined at once, and the corresponding transactions enter the log as the data of each emitted block is obtained. Retrieval terminates, because every block of an emitted sequence, together with its ancestors, is held in full by at least one correct processor — and by at least 2​f+12f+1 whenever the block lies at or below a finalised tip. (Briefly: at least 2​f+12f+1 correct processors DA-voted at or above any finalised tip; a DA-vote requires possession of the block and of its uncertified ancestors down to a certified block; and every certified block, with its ancestors, is held by at least 2​f+12f+1 correct DA-voters, by an induction descending the chain. The weaker one-holder bound concerns only blocks carried by safe-to-extend tips, whose f+1f+1 supporting votes guarantee a single correct holder, on branches later abandoned: possible only under an equivocating producer. The availability lemma of the next subsection gives the full accounting.) A correct processor missing the data of an emitted block requests it from all processors, and after GST a correct holder answers within 2​δ2\delta. The same convention covers the V-QCs of the reference chain, which computing 𝖮𝗋𝖽\mathsf{Ord} requires and which a processor finalising via the pool need not hold: a processor missing a V-QC named by hash requests it from all. Possession is guaranteed, since any leader block on the reference chain of a finalised block received 2​f+12f+1 votes, and the first f+1f+1 correct processors to vote for it necessarily did so via the valid-proposal route (a vote via lines 12–13 presupposes a view V-QC containing f+1f+1 earlier correct votes), each therefore holding the referenced V-QC. In the common case no such retrieval occurs, each view’s referenced V-QC being disseminated with its leader block.

Theorem 2 (Liveness).

If pip_{i} and pjp_{j} are correct and pip_{i} receives the transaction tr\mathrm{tr} then, for some tt, tr∈logj​(t)\mathrm{tr}\in\mathrm{log}_{j}(t).

Proof.

We may suppose tr\mathrm{tr} never enters logj\mathrm{log}_{j}, and derive a contradiction. Throughout, we use the fact that all delays after GST are bounded, so that ‘eventually’ claims compose.

Step 1: tr\mathrm{tr} enters pip_{i}’s chain. We first observe that every block pip_{i} produces is eventually DA-certified, with the certificate eventually held by every correct processor. By induction on height hh: once every correct processor holds the certificate for pip_{i}’s block at height h−1h-1 together with pip_{i}’s block bhb_{h} (which pip_{i} disseminated), the block bhb_{h} is eligible at every correct processor: condition (i) holds since a correct processor’s DA-votes on chain ii are all for blocks of pip_{i}’s unique chain (pip_{i} signs one block per height, and forgeries are excluded), so no conflicting vote exists; (ii) holds with h−h′≤1h-h^{\prime}\leq 1; and (iii) holds along pip_{i}’s chain, the votes below bhb_{h} having been sent in previous steps of the induction. Correct processors DA-vote every eligible block (line 4 of Algorithm 4.2), so pip_{i} receives n−2​fn-2f shares, forms the certificate, and disseminates it. Consequently the window condition of 𝖱𝖾𝖺𝖽𝗒\mathsf{Ready} is satisfied within bounded time whenever it fails, and, since tr∈𝗉𝖾𝗇𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗀\mathrm{tr}\in\mathsf{pending} persistently (it is never included, else Steps 2–3 below apply to the including block), the pacing condition ensures that pip_{i} eventually executes 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝖽𝗎𝖼𝖾𝖭𝖾𝗑𝗍\mathsf{ProduceNext}, producing a block bb containing tr\mathrm{tr}, at height hbh_{b} say.

Step 2: bb is finalised. Let h∗≥hbh^{*}\geq h_{b} be the height of pip_{i}’s tip at some fixed timeslot. Choose t∗≥GSTt^{*}\geq\mathrm{GST} large enough that, by t∗t^{*}, every correct processor has received and DA-voted every block of chain ii up to height h∗h^{*}, and holds every DA-certificate for chain ii up to height h∗−dh^{*}-d. (Such certificates exist: by the window condition, pip_{i} produced its block at height h∗h^{*} only with a certified block at height at least h∗−dh^{*}-d, and certificates are disseminated.) By Corollary 1 and the round-robin 𝗅𝖾𝖺𝖽\mathsf{lead} function, some view vv with correct leader has its first correct entry at a timeslot t≥t∗t\geq t^{*}. By Lemma 11, every correct processor votes for the leader’s block ℓ\ell by t+2​δt+2\delta and finalises it by t+3​δt+3\delta.

Now consider the proposal’s chain ii coordinate. The leader anchors at 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i} or at a DA-certificate of greater height, whichever is higher. It holds certificates for chain ii through height h∗−dh^{*}-d, so the base has height at least h∗−dh^{*}-d. The entries comprise every block the leader has DA-voted extending the base, up to dd of them, and the leader has DA-voted chain ii through height h∗h^{*}. The proposed tip therefore has height at least min⁡{(h∗−d)+d,h∗}=h∗≥hb\min\{(h^{*}-d)+d,\,h^{*}\}=h^{*}\geq h_{b}. If the base itself has height at least h∗h^{*}, then the finalised tip extends the base, which extends bb on the chain’s single path, and we are done. Otherwise every proposed entry at height at most h∗h^{*} lies on the single path and was DA-voted by every correct processor by t∗t^{*}, so every correct voter reports a position of height at least h∗h^{*}. (The leader may also propose entries above h∗h^{*}, which correct voters need not hold; this only lowers reported positions towards the height-h∗h^{*} entry, never below it.) The (3​f+1)(3f+1)-th largest position over the n−fn-f votes of any L-notarisation for ℓ\ell therefore has height at least h∗≥hbh^{*}\geq h_{b}, and the finalised tip extends the block at that position. Since the blocks of chain ii form a single path, bb is an ancestor of the view vv finalised tip on chain ii.

Step 3: bb is emitted. The value 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) computed at view vv may halt before reaching bb’s slot, since some other chain may be unsettled. Let w>vw>v be the next view with correct leader, with first correct entry at a timeslot t′≥tt^{\prime}\geq t (Corollary 1 again). By Lemma 11, every correct processor finalises the view ww block ℓw\ell_{w} by t′+3​δt^{\prime}+3\delta. In doing so it computes 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)=𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q∗)⌢​ρ′\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime})=\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{*})^{\frown}\rho^{\prime}, where Q∗Q^{*} is the V-QC referenced by ℓw\ell_{w}. Now ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation, so ℓ\ell is an ancestor of ℓw\ell_{w} by Lemma 6. The chain of references from ℓw\ell_{w} therefore passes through a V-QC QvQ_{v} for view vv, and 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q∗)⪰𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Qv)\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{*})\succeq\mathsf{Ord}(Q_{v}). By Lemma 7, 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Qv)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q_{v})_{i} extends the view vv finalised tip on chain ii, hence extends bb. Each segment 𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓​(T,T′)\mathsf{Horiz}(T,T^{\prime}) of the recursion defining 𝖮𝗋𝖽\mathsf{Ord} includes every block on T′T^{\prime}’s path in the heights it covers, so bb appears in 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Qv)\mathsf{Ord}(Q_{v}), hence in 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Q∗)\mathsf{Ord}(Q^{*}), hence in 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P′)\mathsf{Emit}(P^{\prime}). Every correct processor therefore emits a sequence of identifiers containing bb by t′+3​δt^{\prime}+3\delta, plus bounded time for any reference-chain V-QCs it must retrieve, and by the retrieval convention it appends the corresponding transactions within bounded further time. (For bb itself no retrieval is needed, since every correct processor holds bb, having DA-voted it.) Either tr\mathrm{tr} was already in its log, as a removed duplicate, or it enters now. In either case tr∈logj\mathrm{tr}\in\mathrm{log}_{j}: a contradiction. ∎

5.3 Remaining properties

We collect the remaining claims made in earlier sections: the availability lemma promised in Section 5.2, membership finality, the block inclusion theorem, and the lower bound forcing the extraction thresholds. Throughout, ‘held in full’ means possession of a block’s complete data (i,h,x,Tr)(i,h,x,\mathrm{Tr}), as opposed to its header or hash, and fa≤ff_{a}\leq f denotes the number of actually faulty processors in the execution at hand.

Availability.

Lemma 12 (Availability).
  1. (a)

    Every certifiable transaction block, and each of its ancestors, is held in full by at least 2​f+12f+1 correct processors (the set of holders may vary from block to block).

  2. (b)

    For every V-notarisation WW and chain ii, the block 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i}, and each of its ancestors, is held in full by at least one correct processor.

  3. (c)

    Every block of an emitted sequence 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) is held in full by at least one correct processor; and by at least 2​f+12f+1 if, on its chain, it lies at or below the finalised tip of some emission, where that tip certifies something new: a position block of rank k∗≥1k^{*}\geq 1, a DA-certified base, or a unanimously supported extension block. (A finalised tip of rank 0 over a hash anchor merely re-affirms the previous safe-to-extend tip, whose supporting votes DA-voted nothing; blocks covered by no other finalisation retain only the single-holder guarantee, which suffices for retrieval.)

Proof.

(a) Let bb be an ancestor of a certifiable block and, among the certifiable blocks extending bb (or equal to it), let b∗b^{*} be one of least height. At least n−2​fn-2f processors DA-voted b∗b^{*}, so at least n−3​f≥2​f+1n-3f\geq 2f+1 correct ones. By condition (iii), each possessed, when it voted, the path from its anchor (a certifiable ancestor of b∗b^{*} of smaller height) to b∗b^{*}. No such anchor has height at least that of bb, since it would then be a certifiable block extending bb (anchors and bb are ancestors of b∗b^{*}, hence comparable) of height smaller than b∗b^{*}’s, contradicting minimality. So each of the 2​f+12f+1 correct voters held bb.

(b) We argue by induction on views. If 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} is a position block 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k_{i}) with ki≥1k_{i}\geq 1, then at least f+1f+1 votes in the tally report π​(i)≥ki\pi(i)\geq k_{i}, so at least one correct processor DA-voted positions 1,…,ki1,\dots,k_{i}, and held, at each vote, the corresponding block and the path down to its certifiable anchor. If the extension carry applies, at least 2​f+12f+1 votes count for 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i}, so at least f+1f+1 correct processors did the same along the carried path. In either case, ancestors below the relevant anchors are covered by (a). If ki=0k_{i}=0 and no carry applies, then 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} is the base itself, which well-formedness requires to be either a DA-certificate, covered by (a), or a hash anchor equal to 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q′)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q^{\prime})_{i} for the V-QC Q′Q^{\prime} referenced by the proposal, which is for an earlier view, and the induction hypothesis applies (the base case being genesis, held by all).

(c) For the stronger claim, suppose the block lies at or below a finalised tip FjF_{j} of one of the three kinds hypothesised, and argue relative to that emission’s pool. If Fj=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,j,kj∗)F_{j}=\mathsf{Prop}(C,j,k^{*}_{j}) with kj∗≥1k^{*}_{j}\geq 1, then at least 3​f+13f+1 votes report π​(j)≥kj∗\pi(j)\geq k^{*}_{j}, so at least 2​f+12f+1 correct processors DA-voted positions 1,…,kj∗1,\dots,k^{*}_{j}; each held any given ancestor bb of FjF_{j} directly, or else had a certifiable anchor extending bb, in which case (a) applies to bb. If FjF_{j} is a DA-certified base, it is certifiable and (a) applies directly. If FjF_{j} is an extension block, all n−fn-f votes count for it, so at least n−2​f≥2​f+1n-2f\geq 2f+1 correct processors DA-voted its path, and the first dichotomy applies. The excluded case, rank 0 over a hash anchor, is exactly the one in which FjF_{j} is the previous safe-to-extend tip re-affirmed, a block that need not be certifiable, so that (a) does not apply. For the weaker claim, note that every block of 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) lies, on its chain, at or below either a finalised tip of the final segment or a coordinate of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌\mathsf{Tips} for some V-QC on the reference chain; a rank-0 hash-anchored finalised tip equals the previous safe-to-extend tip, so in every case (b) applies. ∎

Note the shape of the guarantee: quorum-scale redundancy (2​f+12f+1 correct holders) for everything at or below finalised tips that certify new material, with a single guaranteed holder otherwise. A single correct holder suffices for retrieval (it answers requests after GST), but the redundancy gap is worth quantifying. It concerns, per chain, only the blocks above the last certifiable block or certified base, and its persistence requires a faulty producer, whether equivocating or merely withholding, say by disclosing blocks to a single correct processor. On an honest chain every block is eventually DA-voted by all correct processors (Theorem 2, Step 1), hence certifiable, and (a) restores 2​f+12f+1 holders.

Membership finality.

Order finality of extensions requires unanimity above a fully supported proposal (see the end of this subsection). A useful guarantee is nevertheless available at a much weaker threshold. Say a transaction block bb is membership-finalised by the L-notarisation QQ if bb lies strictly above the base of QQ’s chain proposal for bb’s chain, and at least 3​f+13f+1 of QQ’s votes count for bb.262626The first condition, that bb lie strictly above the base, cannot be dropped. Since ‘counts for’ is closed under ancestry, every vote counts for the base and everything below it, without any voter having DA-voted those blocks, and a carried base needs as little as one correct DA-voter on its branch. Without the condition, an equivocating producer could have a block below the base ‘membership-finalised’ by all n−fn-f votes while n−2​fn-2f correct processors certify an incompatible sibling.

Lemma 13 (Membership finality).

If bb is membership-finalised by some L-notarisation, then no block incompatible with bb is ever certifiable.

Proof.

Suppose b′b^{\prime}, incompatible with bb, were certifiable, diverging from bb’s path at height h0h_{0}, so that at least n−2​f−fan-2f-f_{a} correct processors DA-voted b′b^{\prime}’s path at h0h_{0}. At least 3​f+1−fa3f+1-f_{a} correct processors’ votes count for bb. Consider any one of them, qq say. Since bb lies strictly above the base, qq’s endorsed tip does too, so qq has genuinely DA-voted its endorsed path, from its certified anchor upward, and bb lies on that path. If qq’s anchor has height at least h0h_{0}, the anchor is a certifiable block whose path agrees with bb’s at h0h_{0}, so is incompatible with b′b^{\prime}, and Lemma 1 yields a contradiction with b′b^{\prime}’s certifiability directly. Otherwise qq DA-voted bb’s path at h0h_{0}. If the latter holds for all such qq, then, correct processors DA-voting once per height, the two sets are disjoint, and (3​f+1−fa)+(n−2​f−fa)≤n−fa(3f+1-f_{a})+(n-2f-f_{a})\leq n-f_{a}, i.e. f+1≤faf+1\leq f_{a}, a contradiction. ∎

The threshold is exact, uniformly in faf_{a}. For fault count faf_{a}, the proof shows 2​f+fa+12f+f_{a}+1 counting votes suffice; and 2​f+fa2f+f_{a} do not: with faf_{a} faulty processors, the correct processors can split as 2​f2f DA-voting bb’s branch and n−2​f−fan-2f-f_{a} DA-voting b′b^{\prime}’s, whereupon bb gathers 2​f+fa2f+f_{a} counting votes in an L-notarisation while b′b^{\prime} is certified. Since the protocol must be safe for every fa≤ff_{a}\leq f without knowing faf_{a}, the threshold 3​f+13f+1 is forced, and optimal.

We should be precise about how much the lemma gives, since its conclusion is weaker than it may first appear. Directly, it constrains certification only: every block subsequently certified on the chain is compatible with bb, so the chain’s certified spine can never leave bb’s branch. Since uncertified blocks may nevertheless be finalised, this neither places bb in the ledger nor, on its own, excludes incompatible blocks from the ordering. Both upgrades arrive with larger counts, and we state them for the case that matters below, in which bb’s producer is correct, so that blocks incompatible with bb do not exist at all. When at least n−2​fn-2f votes of every L-notarisation count for bb, which is what Theorem 3 below provides for well-circulated blocks of correct producers, any later finalisation of the chain at or beyond bb’s height extends bb, and places bb with it. Whether the chain is finalised again at such heights is a liveness matter rather than a safety one. For a correct producer this is guaranteed, as in the proof of Theorem 2. A faulty producer, by contrast, may stall its own chain indefinitely, and not only by falling silent: after an equivocation, correct processors that spent their one DA-vote per height on the rival branch are permanently unable to vote for bb’s path below the certified frontier, so that even when a correct holder of bb leads and proposes it, bb’s branch may be able to muster only 3​f+1−fa3f+1-f_{a} correct reported positions, short of the 3​f+13f+1 that finalisation requires unless faulty processors choose to assist. Consistent with damage localisation, the only chain that can be wedged in this way is the equivocator’s own.

Block inclusion.

We now spell out the censorship resistance obtained, which is a pay-off of extension voting. The key point to watch is which quantifiers depend on the leader: none do.

Theorem 3 (Block inclusion).

Let bb be a block on chain ii produced by the correct processor pip_{i}, and let vv be a view in which some leader block ℓ=(v,H​(Q),C)\ell=(v,H(Q),C) receives an L-notarisation. Suppose that:

  1. (i)

    every correct processor DA-voted bb, and each ancestor of bb lying strictly above 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i}, before sending its view vv vote, and;

  2. (ii)

    bb’s height exceeds that of 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i} by at most ee.

Then:

  1. (a)

    the vote of every correct processor that votes for ℓ\ell counts for bb;

  2. (b)

    at least n−2​f≥3​f+1n-2f\geq 3f+1 votes of every L-notarisation for view vv count for bb; in particular, whenever bb lies strictly above the proposal’s base, bb is membership-finalised by every one of them (and when instead a DA-certified base lies at or above bb, every certifiable block is compatible with bb by Lemma 1 in any case);

  3. (c)

    bb is an ancestor of (or equal to) 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} for every view vv V-notarisation WW, and;

  4. (d)

    bb appears in 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) for every pool PP of n−fn-f or more votes for a leader block of any later view that receives an L-notarisation: bb is ordered by the next finalised leader block.

Proof.

Since pip_{i} is correct and signatures cannot be forged, the blocks of chain ii form a single path, one block per height.

(a) Let qq be a correct processor voting for ℓ\ell, with vote (π,ε)(\pi,\varepsilon), and consider the base for chain ii in CC. By proposal validity (checked by the first correct voter, and inherited along the vote-along rule as in Lemma 6), the base extends or equals 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i}. If bb lies at or below the base, then bb is an ancestor of every block qq’s vote endorses on chain ii, and we are done; likewise if the position block 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,π​(i))\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,\pi(i)) lies at or above bb on the chain’s single path, since the endorsed tip extends the position block. Otherwise bb lies above the base, and by (ii) at most ee above 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i}, hence at most ee above the base (which extends 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i}). The position block is a real block of the chain, DA-voted by qq when π​(i)≥1\pi(i)\geq 1 and equal to the base otherwise, and it is an ancestor of bb, since the real entries lie on the chain’s single path below bb. By hypothesis (i), qq has DA-voted every block strictly between 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Q)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q)_{i} and bb, so its DA-voted blocks run consecutively from the position block to bb, and bb lies within ee of the position block. 𝖤𝗑𝗍𝖾𝗇𝗌𝗂𝗈𝗇𝗌​(𝒮,ℓ)\mathsf{Extensions}(\mathcal{S},\ell) therefore carries qq’s endorsed tip on chain ii to bb or beyond, so qq’s vote counts for bb.

(b) An L-notarisation contains votes from n−fn-f distinct processors, at least n−2​fn-2f of them correct. By (a), each such vote counts for bb, and n−2​f≥3​f+1n-2f\geq 3f+1.

(c) Let WW be a view vv V-notarisation with tally ViV_{i}. Correct processors appearing in WW appear with their actual votes. Since ℓ\ell receives an L-notarisation, at least n−2​fn-2f correct processors voted for ℓ\ell, of which at most ff are absent from WW, so at least n−3​f≥2​f+1n-3f\geq 2f+1 votes in ViV_{i} count for bb. If bb lies at or below the position block 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k_{i}), then b⪯𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)ib\preceq\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} immediately. Otherwise bb extends the position block (single path) and has 2​f+12f+1 supporting votes in ViV_{i}, so bb is a carry candidate and the carry applies. Candidates lie on the single path, and a deepest candidate has height at least bb’s, so extends bb: 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(W)i\mathsf{Tips}(W)_{i} extends bb.

(d) Let ℓ′\ell^{\prime}, of view w>vw>v, receive an L-notarisation, and let PP be a pool of n−fn-f or more votes for it. By Lemma 6, ℓ\ell is an ancestor of ℓ′\ell^{\prime}, so the chain of references from ℓ′\ell^{\prime} passes through a V-QC QvQ_{v} for view vv, and 𝖤𝗆𝗂𝗍​(P)\mathsf{Emit}(P) extends 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Qv)\mathsf{Ord}(Q_{v}). By (c), 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Qv)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q_{v})_{i} extends bb. Finally, bb appears in 𝖮𝗋𝖽​(Qv)\mathsf{Ord}(Q_{v}): along QvQ_{v}’s own reference chain the coordinates 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(⋅)i\mathsf{Tips}(\cdot)_{i} are non-decreasing in height (each proposal’s base extends or equals the previous safe-to-extend tip) and all lie on chain ii’s single path, so the 𝖧𝗈𝗋𝗂𝗓\mathsf{Horiz} segments partition the heights below 𝖳𝗂𝗉𝗌​(Qv)i\mathsf{Tips}(Q_{v})_{i}, and bb is appended in the segment covering its height. ∎

One addition is available when the leader proposes honestly for chain ii, and we state it separately because, unlike everything in the theorem, its hypotheses depend on the leader.

Corollary 2.

In the setting of Theorem 3, suppose additionally that bb is compatible with the proposed tip for chain ii.

  1. (a)

    If bb lies at or below the proposed tip, then the finalised tip on chain ii extracted from every L-notarisation for view vv, and from every pool of n−fn-f or more view vv votes, extends bb.

  2. (b)

    If bb extends the proposed tip, the same holds for every pool containing the votes of all correct processors (though not necessarily for every individual L-notarisation, whose unanimity ff faulty votes can deny).

In either case bb is finalised within the view, although its placement in the total ordering may await a later view.

Proof.

(a) If bb lies at or below the base, then every extracted tip extends the base, which is position 0, and hence extends bb. Otherwise write b=𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,m)b=\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,m), for some m≤mim\leq m_{i}. The proposed entries below bb are ancestors of bb lying above the base, so by hypothesis (i) of the theorem every correct voter has DA-voted 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,k)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k) for every k∈[1,m]k\in[1,m], and reports π​(i)≥m\pi(i)\geq m. Every L-notarisation therefore contains at least n−2​f≥3​f+1n-2f\geq 3f+1 votes with π​(i)≥m\pi(i)\geq m, so its position rank ki∗k^{*}_{i} is at least mm, and the same holds for the rank of any pool of n−fn-f or more votes. The extracted tip is 𝖯𝗋𝗈𝗉​(C,i,ki∗)\mathsf{Prop}(C,i,k^{*}_{i}) or a block extending it, and so extends bb.

(b) If bb extends the proposed tip, then every proposed entry is an ancestor of bb lying above the base, so every correct processor that votes for ℓ\ell reports π​(i)=mi\pi(i)=m_{i}, and by Theorem 3(a) its vote counts for bb. A pool containing the votes of all correct processors thus contains at least n−fn-f votes with π​(i)=mi\pi(i)=m_{i}, giving position rank ki∗=mik^{*}_{i}=m_{i}, and at least n−fn-f votes counting for bb, so the extension step applies and FiF_{i} is a deepest block that n−fn-f of the pool’s votes count for. Any two such blocks are compatible, since their supporting sets intersect in a correct processor, whose DA-votes determine a single path; a deepest one therefore extends bb.

In either case, placement may await a later view, since emission halts at the empty slots of unsettled chains (Section 4). ∎

Part (a)’s additional hypothesis is exactly what junk entries deny (Section 3.7): the one thing a leader can withhold is this in-view finalisation, never the membership and carry guarantees of the theorem. Part (b) makes formal the observation of Section 3 that the unanimity required for extension finality is unanimity within a single L-QC, and that an L-QC with the required unanimity can always be assembled from the pool once the correct votes have arrived, whatever the ff faulty voters do.

What the theorem gives.

Hypotheses (i) and (ii) mention only dissemination: (i) holds whenever bb and its predecessors reach the correct processors before they vote (correct processors DA-vote eligible blocks immediately, so one δ\delta of dissemination suffices), and (ii) is a freshness bound, satisfied by everything produced since the previous view’s tips up to depth ee. Neither hypothesis mentions the leader, and the conclusions quantify over every L-notarisation and every V-notarisation of the view. The view vv leader — by junk entries, stale entries, a low anchor, equivocation, or any other behaviour — can influence which of these objects exist, but not what they contain regarding bb. The consequence is best put as a dichotomy: either view vv produces no L-notarisation at all, or bb is membership-finalised in view vv and ordered by the next finalised leader block. A Byzantine leader cannot have its block finalised and exclude a well-circulated honest block.
